question: What does stage 3's HTTP API add on top of the QueuedNotifier, and what does "an API for services, not browsers" mean here?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 1 aur 2 ek library the: `QueuedNotifier.notify()` ko wahi call kar sakta tha jo same process mein import kare. Stage 3 uske aage ek Express app rakhta hai taaki doosri services -- order service, auth service -- HTTP par notification maang sakein: `POST /notifications` (Idempotency-Key header + `{ typeId, userId, data }`), `GET /notifications/:id`, `GET/PUT /users/:userId/preferences`, aur providers ke liye `POST /webhooks/:channel`.

"Services ke liye, browsers ke liye nahi" ka matlab teen concrete cheezein hain. Pehli: auth ek shared API key hai (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`), koi user login, session ya cookie nahi. Doosri: koi CORS nahi -- browser se seedha call karna design mein hi nahi hai. Teesri: caller ek trusted backend hai, isliye `userId` body mein aata hai aur API maan leti hai ki caller ne end user ko pehle hi check kar liya hai. PLAN.md seedha bolta hai: ek open notification API free SMS-spam service hai, isliye koi "no auth" mode nahi hai.

Handlers patle hain: shape check, phir library call, phir status code. Saare business rules (preferences, quiet hours, fallback, retries) library mein hi rehte hain, HTTP layer unhe duplicate nahi karti. `npm start` (`src/main.ts`) API ke saath ek worker bhi chalata hai, fake senders aur demo user `u1` ke saath -- kuch bhi process se bahar nahi jaata. Interview mein point: HTTP ek transport hai, logic ka owner library hai.
why_needed: Library sirf ek process ke andar kaam aati hai. Real system mein notification maangne wali services alag processes / alag teams hoti hain, unhe ek network contract chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant ki kitchen (library) pehle se ready hai; HTTP API uski service window hai jahan sirf registered delivery partners (services) apna token dikha ke order dete hain -- seedha customers (browsers) wahan nahi aate.
how_it_works: `createApp(options)` ek Express app banata hai: pehle webhook route, phir API-key middleware, phir `express.json`, phir routes, phir 404 fallback, phir error handler. Har route library ka synchronous method call karta hai aur result ko JSON + status mein badalta hai.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts` ki header comment saare endpoints aur status codes list karti hai. `AppOptions` mein `apiKey` required hai ("there is no open mode"), `bodyLimit` default "64kb", `webhookSecrets`, `clock`, `log`. `src/main.ts` env se `NOTIFY_API_KEY`, `PORT` (3000), `HOST` (default 127.0.0.1) padhta hai. Tests: `test/http.test.ts` real Express ko random port par chala ke Node ke `fetch` se call karta hai.

// real, README.md (Stage 3: HTTP API)
NOTIFY_API_KEY=<at least 16 characters> PORT=3000 npm start   # API + a worker, fake senders, demo user u1

curl -i -X POST localhost:3000/notifications \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTIFY_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Idempotency-Key: login-7f3a" \
  -d '{"typeId":"otp","userId":"u1","data":{"code":"482913"}}'
# 202 Accepted, Location: /notifications/<id>

Business logic ek jagah (library), HTTP layer patli
Auth hamesha on -- open mode exist hi nahi karta
disadvantages: Ek shared key: caller-wise permissions ya audit nahi
End user ki identity check caller ki zimmedari hai
In memory: process restart = data gone

Browser se seedha call allow karne ke liye CORS khol dena
Dev ke liye 'auth off' flag chhod dena jo production tak pahunch jaaye

question: Why is "sent" not the same as "delivered", and what is a delivery receipt?
answer_hinglish:
Jab hamara worker provider (SES, Twilio, FCM jaisa) ko message deta hai aur woh 200 bolta hai, toh uska matlab sirf itna hai: provider ne message ACCEPT kar liya. User tak pahuncha ya nahi, woh baad mein pata chalta hai -- SMS carrier ne number galat bataya, email ka mailbox exist nahi karta, phone off tha. Provider yeh khabar baad mein ek webhook se bhejta hai: yahi delivery receipt hai.

Is project mein `src/receipts.ts` ke top comment mein yahi likha hai: "sent only means the provider ACCEPTED the message". Do events hain: `delivered` aur `bounced`. Provider `POST /webhooks/<channel>` par `{ providerId, event, occurredAt }` bhejta hai, signed. Receipt delivery par `receipt: { event, at }` ban ke dikhta hai `GET /notifications/:id` mein.

Iska asar status par bhi hai: `notificationStatus()` (record.ts) mein ek sent delivery jiska receipt `bounced` hai, woh `failed` count hoti hai. Agar koi doosra channel sent hai aur bounce nahi hua, notification phir bhi `delivered` hai.

Kya NAHI bana, honestly: bounce ke baad agle channel par fallback, suppression list (bounced address par dobara mat bhejo), aur `opened` / `clicked` events. Interview mein yeh distinction important hai kyunki "delivery rate" dashboards aksar provider acceptance ko delivery samajh lete hain.
why_needed: Bina receipt ke system ko lagta hai OTP pahunch gaya jabki number galat tha. Support, metrics aur future fallback sab is ek fact par depend karte hain.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko parcel de diya (sent) aur courier ka 'delivered, signed by X' SMS aana (receipt) -- do alag moments hain. Beech mein parcel wapas bhi aa sakta hai (bounce).
how_it_works: Provider message accept karke ek provider id deta hai; worker woh id delivery par likhta hai. Baad mein provider webhook mein wahi id bhejta hai; `applyReceipt(channel, providerId, receipt)` id se delivery dhoondh ke receipt merge karta hai.
in_this_project: `src/receipts.ts` mein `RECEIPT_EVENTS = ["delivered", "bounced"]`, `Receipt { event, at }`. `src/record.ts` ka `notificationStatus` sent + bounced ko failed maanta hai. `test/receipts.test.ts` ka test 'a bounce makes the notification failed unless another channel still counts as delivered' push bounce par status delivered (email sent) aur email bhi bounce hone par failed check karta hai.
advantages: Status sach ke kareeb (bounce = failed)
Support ko pata chalta hai kya hua
Future fallback / suppression ka base
disadvantages: Ek aur inbound endpoint secure karna padta hai
Receipts late, duplicate, out of order aate hain
Opened/clicked jaise events yahan nahi hain
common_mistakes: Provider ka 200 ko delivered maan lena
Bounce ko ignore karna aur baar baar same bad address par bhejna
Receipt ko provider id ke bina match karne ki koshish

question: How does POST /notifications make retries safe over HTTP, and what do 202, 200 with Idempotent-Replayed and 409 mean?
answer_hinglish:
Network unreliable hai: order service ne OTP request bheji, response timeout ho gaya, usne retry kiya. Agar server har request ko naya maane toh user ko do OTP jaayenge. Isliye `Idempotency-Key` header REQUIRED hai -- na ho toh 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` "Idempotency-Key header is required". Key 1 se 255 characters, `checkRequest` (planner.ts) check karta hai.

Teen answers hain. **202 Accepted + `Location: /notifications/<id>`**: naya request, record bana aur jobs queue hui -- abhi bheja nahi gaya, isliye 201 ya 200 nahi, 202. **200 + `Idempotent-Replayed: true`**: same key, same body pehle aa chuka; wahi record lauta, kuch naya queue nahi hua (header name Stripe wala). **409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`**: same key, alag body -- yeh caller ka bug hai, "first one wins" chupchaap karna galat hota.

Same body ka matlab: `typeId`, `userId`, `data` ka stable fingerprint (`stableStringify`), toh JSON key order se farak nahi padta. Ek aur rule library se aata hai: error ka matlab kuch store nahi hua, key abhi bhi free hai. Test 'malformed requests -> 400 ... the key is still free' nau galat requests ke baad `k1` se 202 paata hai.

Limit: keys cache-kit LRU mein 24 h TTL ke saath hain (stage 2). Uske baad same key naya notification banayegi -- Stripe jaisa hi trade-off.
why_needed: Retries ke bina reliable client nahi banta, aur bina idempotency ke retry duplicate OTP / duplicate charge banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank counter par token number: wahi token dobara dikhao toh clerk wahi receipt dobara de deta hai, naya transaction nahi karta. Wahi token kisi aur amount ke saath dikhao toh clerk mana kar deta hai.
how_it_works: Handler pehle `getByKey(key)` dekhta hai, phir `notify()`. notify andar fingerprint compare karta hai: match = existing record, mismatch = throw 409. Handler before/after ids compare karke 202 ya 200 chunta hai.
in_this_project: `app.post("/notifications")` in `src/http/app.ts`: `res.status(200).set("Idempotent-Replayed", "true")` replay ke liye, `res.status(202).location(...)` naye ke liye. Tests: 'the same key and body again -> 200, Idempotent-Replayed, the same record, nothing queued' (`queue.size` 1 hi rehta hai), 'the same key with a different body -> 409; the first record is untouched'.
advantages: Client blindly retry kar sakta hai
Caller ko pata chalta hai replay hua ya naya
Conflict ek loud error hai, silent bug nahi
disadvantages: Key 24 h baad bhool jaati hai
Caller ko key generate karni padti hai
In memory: multi-instance par shared store chahiye
common_mistakes: Key optional rakhna
Body compare na karna (alag request ko replay maan lena)
Failed request par key 'use' mark kar dena

question: How does the API choose status codes "by whose fault it is", and why one error shape?
answer_hinglish:
Rule simple hai: status code caller ko batata hai ki galti kiski hai aur retry karne se kuch badlega ya nahi. **400** request hi malformed hai -- bad JSON (`INVALID_JSON`), header missing, field ka galat type (`INVALID_REQUEST`). **401** key nahi ya galat. **404** URL wala resource nahi (notification id, user, route). **409** idempotency conflict. **413** body 64 KB se badi. **415** Content-Type JSON nahi. **422** request well-formed hai par impossible: `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, `UNKNOWN_USER`, `TEMPLATE_VARIABLE_MISSING`, `INVALID_PREFERENCES`. **500** hamari galti -- jaise `NO_SENDER` (server par us channel ka sender configure hi nahi) -- message chhupa ke `{ code: "INTERNAL", message: "internal error" }`, asli error log mein.

400 vs 422 ka farak interview mein poocha jaata hai: 400 matlab parse / shape hi galat, 422 matlab shape sahi par meaning galat (aisa type exist hi nahi karta). Dono 4xx hain, toh same request ka retry bekaar hai; 500 par retry samajh mein aata hai.

Shape ek hi: `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`. Caller `code` par switch karta hai, message human ke liye hai aur badal sakta hai. Mapping ek jagah hai: `STATUS_BY_CODE` (library ke `NotificationErrorCode` se status) aur `toHttp()` jo HttpError, NotificationError aur body-parser errors sab ko isi shape mein laata hai. Mutation checks mein '422s turned into 400s' aur 'a 500 message not hidden' dono pakde gaye.
why_needed: Caller ka retry logic aur alerting status code par chalta hai. Galat code (sab 400 ya sab 500) ya toh bekaar retries karwata hai ya asli bugs chhupata hai.
real_world_analogy: Hospital reception: 'form galat bhara' (400), 'ID card nahi' (401), 'yeh doctor yahan nahi baithte' (422), 'hamari machine kharab hai, baad mein aao' (500). Har jawab ka next step alag.
how_it_works: Har throw error handler tak jaata hai; `toHttp(error, log)` type dekh ke `{ status, code, message }` banata hai; status >= 500 par log + generic message.
in_this_project: `STATUS_BY_CODE` in `src/http/app.ts`: `NO_SENDER: 500`, `INVALID_TYPE: 500`, `DUPLICATE_TYPE: 500` (catalog errors startup par hote hain, request se nahi). Tests: 'well-formed but impossible -> 422; nothing stored', 'a channel with no sender is a 500 with the message hidden, and it is logged' (`logged[0].code` NO_SENDER), 'unknown notification, unknown user, unknown route -> 404 JSON'.
advantages: Caller ka retry decision status se ho jaata hai
Ek shape: ek client-side error parser
Internal details leak nahi hote
disadvantages: 400 vs 422 par teams mein bahas hoti hai -- documented rule chahiye
Generic 500 message debugging ke liye log par depend karta hai
common_mistakes: Har error par 500 ya har error par 400
Stack trace response mein bhejna
Har route ka apna error format

question: Why does the receipt merge rule (delivered < bounced, ties keep the earlier time) replace a store of seen event ids?
answer_hinglish:
Webhooks teen tarah se bigadte hain: late aate hain, do baar aate hain, aur out of order aate hain. Common jawab hai har event id ka ek "seen" store rakho aur duplicate ignore karo. Is project ne doosra raasta liya: receipt state ko hi aisa banaya ki order aur duplicates se farak hi na pade.

`mergeReceipt(current, incoming)` ka rule: higher rank jeetta hai (`delivered` = 1, `bounced` = 2); same rank par earlier `at` rehta hai. Yeh ek "maximum" hai, aur maximum teen properties rakhta hai: associative, commutative, idempotent. Matlab `merge(merge(a, b), c)` har order mein same, aur `merge(a, a) = a`. Toh final state = jitne bhi events aaye unka max -- kisi bhi order mein, kitne bhi copies ke saath. (Distributed systems mein isse join-semilattice / CRDT-style merge bolte hain.)

Bounced upar kyun? Email ko receiving server accept kar sakta hai ("delivered") aur baad mein bounce kar sakta hai; ek late `delivered` kabhi bounce ko undo nahi kar sakta. Tie par earlier time kyun? Pehli baar kab hua woh fact hai; later copy ek retry hai.

Seen-ids store se better kyun: koi extra store / TTL nahi, aur yeh un events ko bhi handle karta hai jo DISTINCT hain par ulte order mein aaye -- dedup woh solve hi nahi karta. Proof: `test/receipts.test.ts` ka randomized test, 300 event lists, har ek 5 baar shuffle + duplicates, independent expected answer se compare. Unchanged ko same object lauta ke detect kiya jaata hai (`toBe(x)`).
why_needed: Providers at-least-once deliver karte hain aur ordering guarantee nahi dete. Bina iske state flip-flop karegi ya duplicate store ko hamesha ke liye grow karna padega.
real_world_analogy: Exam ka highest score record karna: copies kitni bhi aayein, kisi bhi order mein, max wahi rehta hai. Last-written-wins jaisa nahi jahan late aaya purana paper result bigaad de.
how_it_works: RANK table se compare; unequal rank par bada wala; equal par chhota `at`. Agar current hi jeeta toh `current` object hi return -- caller `merged === delivery.receipt` se 'unchanged' samajhta hai.
in_this_project: `src/receipts.ts`: `const RANK = { delivered: 1, bounced: 2 }`, `mergeReceipt`. `QueuedNotifier.applyReceipt` same rule parked receipts par bhi lagata hai. Mutation checks (24, sab pakde): 'ranking reversed', 'tie keeps the later time', 'last event wins', 'unchanged not detected (a copy instead of the same object)'. README: ek test pehle delivered phir bounced bhejta tha jo 'last one wins' bhi pass kar deta; ab bounced pehle bhejta hai.
advantages: Order aur duplicates dono ek rule se handle
Koi seen-ids store nahi, koi TTL nahi
Randomized test se property-level proof
disadvantages: Sirf totally ordered events ke liye kaam karta hai
Agar ek event legitimately state ko 'neeche' le jaaye (re-delivered after bounce) toh model badalna padega
Har event ki history nahi bachti, sirf max
common_mistakes: Last-write-wins use karna (late delivered bounce mita deta)
Event ids dedup ko order problem ka solution samajhna
Tie par later time rakhna
follow_up_questions: Where would this ranking break if you added opened and clicked?
What is a join-semilattice and why does it fit here?
When would you still need an event-id dedup store?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Data-driven merge extra storage bachata hai par har naye event type ko ek total order mein fit karna padta hai. Opened/clicked bounce ke saath ek line mein nahi aate -- unke liye alag fields (har ek ka apna max) chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Provider ka `occurredAt` galat ya clock skewed ho toh tie-break galat time rakh sakta hai, par event (rank) phir bhi sahi rehta hai. Agar provider ek bounce galti se bhej de toh koi 'undo' nahi hai.
advanced.alternatives: Event-id dedup table (unique constraint), version numbers per delivery, ya poora event log store karke state recompute karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Rule O(1) aur stateless hai, toh 100x webhook volume par bhi merge sasta hai; bottleneck record lookup aur write hoga, merge nahi. DB mein yeh ek conditional UPDATE ban jaata hai (rank compare in WHERE).
advanced.production_improvements: Raw events ek append-only log mein bhi rakho (audit / debugging), state max se derive karo; opened/clicked ke liye per-event-type max fields; provider-specific event names ko is ranking mein map karne wala adapter.

question: How does the POST handler tell a new request from a replay, and why is calling getByKey just before notify() safe?
answer_hinglish:
`notify()` dono cases mein record hi lautata hai -- naya ho ya replay. HTTP ko farak chahiye (202 vs 200), par library ka return type isse nahi batata. Trick: handler `notify()` se theek pehle `notifier.getByKey(idempotencyKey)` call karta hai. Agar key pehle se thi, `before` wahi record hai aur `notify()` bhi wahi id lautata hai -> replay, 200. Agar `before` undefined tha, toh is request ne record banaya -> 202.

Yeh safe kyun hai? Dono calls synchronous hain. Node single-threaded event loop par chalta hai: ek synchronous code block ke beech mein koi doosra request handler run nahi kar sakta. Toh `getByKey` aur `notify` ke beech koi doosra request same key register nahi kar sakta. Code comment yahi bolta hai: "Both calls are synchronous, so nothing can run between them".

Detail: `getByKey` andar `this.keys.peek(...)` use karta hai, `get` nahi -- peek LRU order nahi chhoota, sirf dekhta hai. Conflict case mein `notify()` khud 409 throw karta hai, toh handler ko kuch compare nahi karna.

Yeh assumption tootegi jab store async ho jaaye (Redis / DB): `await getByKey` aur `await notify` ke beech doosra request aa sakta hai. Tab sahi tareeka hai `notify()` khud `{ record, created: boolean }` lautaye, atomic insert (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`) ke result se. Mutation 'replay not detected' test ne pakda.
why_needed: API ko 202 aur 200 alag dene hain bina library ka contract badle. Galat detect karne se client ko lagega request naya tha ya replay -- monitoring aur client logic dono galat.
real_world_analogy: Register mein naam pehle se hai ya nahi dekho, phir sign karwao -- jab tak counter par ek hi aadmi khada hai (single thread), beech mein koi aur naam nahi likh sakta.
how_it_works: before = getByKey(key) -> record = notify(req) -> before?.id === record.id ? 200 : 202. 409 notify ke andar se throw.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts` POST handler; `QueuedNotifier.getByKey` in `src/queued-notifier.ts` (`this.keys.peek`). PLAN.md stage 3: "New vs replay is decided by a getByKey just before notify(): both synchronous, nothing can run between them." Test 'the same key and body again -> 200, Idempotent-Replayed, the same record, nothing queued'.

Race-free jab tak dono sync hain
Simple, do line ka logic
disadvantages: Ek hidden assumption (synchronous) par tika hai
Async store par yeh pattern race ban jaata hai
common_mistakes: Beech mein ek `await` daal dena (race khul jaata hai)
Response body compare karke replay detect karna
`get` use karke LRU order bina wajah badalna

question: Walk through toHttp(): how do HttpError, NotificationError and body-parser errors all end up as one JSON error?
answer_hinglish:
Express mein har synchronous throw (aur `next(err)`) us middleware tak jaata hai jiske chaar arguments hain -- woh error handler hai. Yahan woh handler bas `toHttp(error, log)` call karke `res.status(status).json({ error: { code, message } })` karta hai. Saara decision `toHttp` mein hai, chaar branches:

1. **HttpError** (HTTP layer ka apna error, file-private class): status aur code already set hain -- 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 404 NOT_FOUND, 415, 400 INVALID_REQUEST, webhook ke INVALID_SIGNATURE / INVALID_RECEIPT. Seedha return.
2. **NotificationError** (library): `STATUS_BY_CODE[error.code] ?? 500`. Agar status >= 500 (NO_SENDER etc.) toh log karo aur `INTERNAL` / "internal error" lautao -- asli message chhupa.
3. **body-parser errors**: unke paas `type` field hota hai. `entity.parse.failed` -> 400 INVALID_JSON, `entity.too.large` -> 413 BODY_TOO_LARGE, `encoding.unsupported` / `charset.unsupported` -> 415 UNSUPPORTED_ENCODING.
4. **Baaki sab** (TypeError, programming bug): log + 500 INTERNAL.

Design points: library errors HTTP nahi jaanti (library kisi bhi transport mein chal sakti hai), mapping ek table mein hai; `Record<NotificationErrorCode, number>` TypeScript ko force karta hai ki naya error code bina status ke compile na ho. Default branch hamesha 500 + log hai, toh koi naya unknown error kabhi galti se 4xx nahi banta ya leak nahi hota. Test 'an unexpected throw is a 500 with the message hidden' ek fake notifier se "secret detail" throw karwata hai aur check karta hai ki response mein "secret" nahi hai par log mein hai.
why_needed: Error handling bikhri ho toh kahin stack trace leak hota hai, kahin galat status. Ek function = ek jagah review aur test.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi complaint desk jahan har department ki shikayat aati hai; desk wala ek chart (STATUS_BY_CODE) dekh ke category likhta hai, aur andar ki gadbad (500) public ko nahi batata, sirf register mein likhta hai.
how_it_works: Order: instanceof HttpError -> instanceof NotificationError -> body-parser `type` -> default. Log sirf 500 cases mein.
in_this_project: `toHttp` aur `HttpError` `src/http/app.ts` mein; error handler `app.use((error, _req, res, _next) => ...)` sab routes aur 404 fallback ke baad registered. Mutation checks: 'a 500 message not hidden', 'body-parser errors not mapped' -- dono pakde. Test 'malformed requests -> 400' mein `{"typeId":` raw body INVALID_JSON deta hai; '... over the body limit -> 413' `bodyLimit: "1kb"` ke saath.

Unknown errors hamesha 500 + log (fail safe)
Library transport-agnostic rehti hai
disadvantages: body-parser ke `type` strings par dependency (upgrade par check karna padega)
Log function inject karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Error handler ko teen arguments ka likhna (Express use normal middleware samjhega)
Default branch mein error.message bhej dena
Library errors mein HTTP status daal dena

advanced.failure_scenarios: Body-parser ka naya error type (upgrade ke baad) default branch mein 500 ban jaayega -- safe direction mein galti, par caller ko 4xx milna chahiye tha. Log function khud throw kare toh response atak sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Express 5 (async errors native), ek `asyncHandler` wrapper, ya Fastify jiska schema-based error handling built-in hai. RFC 9457 problem+json format bhi ek standard shape option hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Volume badhne se mapping cost nahi badhti; badhta hai log volume -- 500s ko structured logs + request id + rate-limited alerting chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Har response mein request id header, structured JSON logs, 500 ka metric/alert, aur problem+json ya documented error codes ki list jo client SDK generate kare.

question: What does QueuedNotifier.applyReceipt do, and what are sentBy and parked?
answer_hinglish:
`applyReceipt(channel, providerId, receipt)` webhook route se call hota hai aur teen mein se ek outcome lautata hai: `applied`, `unchanged`, ya `parked`. Synchronous hai, `notify()` jaisa.

Andar do maps hain. **`sentBy`**: ek `Map<string, string>`, key `"<channel>:<providerId>"`, value record id. Jab worker ek successful send record karta hai, har accepted provider id ke liye entry daalta hai (push ke kai devices ho sakte hain, har device ki apni id). **`parked`**: cache-kit ka `LruCache<string, Receipt>`, default 10 000 entries aur 1 h TTL, un receipts ke liye jo send record hone se pehle aa gaye.

Flow: key banao -> `sentBy` se record id -> record mein us channel ki delivery dhoondo. Delivery nahi mili toh parked mein `mergeReceipt(parked.get(key), receipt)` set karo -> `parked` (HTTP 202). Mili toh `mergeReceipt(delivery.receipt, receipt)`; agar result wahi object hai jo pehle tha -> `unchanged` (200), warna assign karke `applied` (200). Stats counters `receiptsApplied`, `receiptsUnchanged`, `receiptsParked` badhte hain.

Send side par (worker ka sent branch): `sentBy.set(key, record.id)`, phir `parked.get(key)` -- kuch tha toh merge, `parked.delete(key)`, `receiptsApplied++`.

Honest gap: `sentBy` kabhi trim nahi hota, records ki tarah hi badhta hai (README mein documented). Unknown ids parked mein TTL ke baad expire ho jaati hain.
why_needed: Webhook sirf provider id deta hai; hamein usse record tak pahunchne ka index chahiye, aur jo receipt jaldi aa gaya use kho na dein.

question: One process runs the API, the worker and the webhook endpoint. How would you split this for production, and what stays the same?
answer_hinglish:
Abhi `startServer(app, worker, ...)` ek hi Node process mein Express app aur ek `Worker` chalata hai, aur dono same in-memory `QueuedNotifier` share karte hain -- records, idempotency keys, queue, `sentBy`, parked receipts sab ek heap mein. Demo aur tests ke liye yeh simplest sahi cheez hai, aur README honestly kehta hai queued jobs process ke saath chale jaate hain.

Production mein main teen deployable units banaunga. **API tier** (stateless, load balancer ke peeche, N replicas): auth, shape checks, `notify()` jo ek durable store mein record + idempotency key ek transaction mein likhe aur ek real queue (SQS / RabbitMQ / Kafka ya DB outbox) mein job daale. **Worker tier** (alag autoscaling, queue depth par): claim with lease, provider call, result likhna -- stage 2 ka lease token check waisa hi. **Webhook ingress** (alag route ya alag service): providers ke bursts API ko slow na karein; signature verify, phir receipt apply ya ek queue mein daal ke async apply.

Kya same rehta hai: library ke contracts. Leases aur provider idempotency key `<id>:<channel>` already at-least-once maan ke bane hain; receipt merge already order-independent hai, toh multi-instance webhook handlers ko coordination nahi chahiye -- bas DB mein conditional update. Kya badalta hai: getByKey-before-notify trick (sync assumption) ko atomic insert se replace karna, parked receipts ko shared store (DB table with expiry) mein le jaana, aur shutdown ka matlab "stop claiming" ho jaata hai, kyunki jobs ab durable hain.
why_needed: Interview mein HLD follow-up yahi hota hai: LLD toh sahi hai, ab 1M users aur multiple machines par kya karoge.
real_world_analogy: Chhoti dukaan mein ek hi aadmi order leta, khana banata aur delivery ki khabar sunta hai. Badi chain mein counter, kitchen aur delivery desk alag log hain, par recipe (library rules) wahi rehti hai.
how_it_works: Abhi: HTTP -> notifier (memory) -> queue (memory) -> worker (same process). Baad mein: HTTP replicas -> DB + queue -> worker replicas -> providers -> webhook ingress -> DB.
in_this_project: `src/http/server.ts` (`startServer`), `src/main.ts` (wiring: catalog, `InMemoryUsers`, `InMemoryJobQueue`, `FakeSender`s, `InboxSender`). server.ts comment: "Jobs still queued stay queued -- with a real queue another process picks them up; in memory they are lost with the process (documented)." PLAN.md stage 3: "One process runs the API and a worker".
advantages: Abhi ka design simple aur poora testable
Library contracts (leases, provider keys, merge) multi-instance ke liye pehle se tayaar
Split karne par tiers alag scale hote hain
disadvantages: Ek process = single point of failure, data volatile
Split ke baad ops cost: queue, DB, deployment
common_mistakes: Multiple API replicas chala dena jabki state in memory hai
Worker ko API process mein hi scale karna
Webhook bursts ko main API ke saath mix karna
follow_up_questions: Where would you put the idempotency key store?
How does graceful shutdown change once jobs are durable?
Would you apply receipts synchronously or via a queue?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek process: zero infra, consistent memory, par HA nahi. Split: har tier independent scale/deploy, par distributed consistency (idempotency, receipts) ab DB constraints se aani padegi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: API replica down: LB doosre par bhejta hai, client idempotency key se retry karta hai. Worker crash: lease expire, job wapas. Webhook service down: providers retry karte hain (zyada tar), par sab nahi -- isliye ingress ko highly available aur patla rakho.
advanced.alternatives: Monolith with multiple replicas + DB-backed queue (outbox, SKIP LOCKED) chhote scale ke liye kaafi hai; bade scale par Kafka partitions per user, ya managed services (SNS/Pinpoint).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: DB-backed queue + worker replicas. 100x: partitioned queue, per-channel worker pools, provider rate limits per pool, receipts ka async pipeline, records ka retention/archival.

question: Everything here is in memory. How would you model notifications, idempotency keys and receipts in a relational database?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest baat: is project mein koi database nahi hai -- records `Map` mein, keys cache-kit LRU mein, `sentBy` ek `Map`, parked receipts ek LRU. Par in sab ka shape seedha tables mein map hota hai, aur code ke rules DB constraints ban jaate hain.

**notifications**: `id`, `type_id`, `user_id`, `category`, `mode`, `created_at`. **idempotency_keys**: `key` PRIMARY KEY, `fingerprint`, `notification_id`, `expires_at` (24 h). New vs replay: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING RETURNING notification_id` -- row mili toh naya (202), nahi mili toh existing padho aur fingerprint compare (200 ya 409). Yeh getByKey-before-notify ka atomic version hai; notification + key + jobs ek transaction mein.

**deliveries**: `notification_id`, `channel`, `status`, `provider_id`, `receipt_event`, `receipt_rank`, `receipt_at`. Index `UNIQUE (channel, provider_id)` -- yahi `sentBy` map hai, aur channel isliye kyunki provider ids sirf provider ke andar unique hain.

**Receipt merge as SQL**: `UPDATE deliveries SET receipt_event = $e, receipt_rank = $r, receipt_at = $at WHERE channel = $c AND provider_id = $p AND (receipt_rank IS NULL OR $r > receipt_rank OR ($r = receipt_rank AND $at < receipt_at))`. 0 rows updated aur row exist karti hai -> unchanged; row hi nahi -> park. Concurrent webhooks ke liye yeh ek atomic compare-and-set hai, koi lock nahi.

**parked_receipts**: same columns + `expires_at`, ek cleanup job. Insert-or-merge `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE` same rank condition ke saath.
why_needed: Interviewer zaroor poochega 'restart par kya hoga' aur 'do replicas par'. Jawab schema aur constraints mein hai.
real_world_analogy: Register (in-memory map) ko ek bank ledger mein badalna: har rule (ek token ek baar, ek tracking number ek parcel) ab ledger ke format mein likha hai, kisi clerk ki yaad mein nahi.
how_it_works: Unique constraints idempotency aur provider-id index sambhalte hain; conditional UPDATE merge rule ko atomic banata hai; TTL columns + cleanup LRU/TTL ko replace karte hain.
in_this_project: Code ke equivalents: `QueuedNotifier` ke `records`, `keys` (LRU 24 h), `sentBy` (`"<channel>:<providerId>"`), `parked` (LRU 1 h, 10 000). `mergeReceipt` ka rank/tie rule SQL WHERE mein. README receipts section: "the provider-index (sentBy) is never trimmed (it grows like the records)" -- DB mein yeh retention policy se solve hota.

-- illustrative, not in the repo: the merge rule as one atomic UPDATE (PostgreSQL)
UPDATE deliveries
   SET receipt_event = $1, receipt_rank = $2, receipt_at = $3
 WHERE channel = $4 AND provider_id = $5
   AND (receipt_rank IS NULL
        OR $2 > receipt_rank
        OR ($2 = receipt_rank AND $3 < receipt_at));
-- 1 row: applied; 0 rows and the delivery exists: unchanged; no delivery: park it

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX deliveries_provider ON deliveries (channel, provider_id);

Constraints race conditions khatam karte hain
Merge rule lock-free CAS ban jaata hai
disadvantages: Har webhook ek DB write
Retention/archival plan chahiye (records, keys, parked)
Hot table par index maintenance
common_mistakes: Idempotency check aur insert alag queries mein (race)
provider_id par akela unique index (channel bhool jaana)
Receipt ko blind UPDATE se overwrite karna
follow_up_questions: How would you clean up expired idempotency keys without locking the table?
Would you store raw webhook events too?

advanced.failure_scenarios: DB slow / down: API 503 de, client idempotency key se retry kare. Partial write se bachne ke liye notification + key + outbox ek transaction. Cleanup job ruk gaya toh keys table badhta jaayega.
advanced.alternatives: Redis `SET NX EX` idempotency ke liye, DynamoDB conditional `UpdateItem` merge ke liye, ya event-sourced receipts table.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: indexes + partitioning by created_at. 100x: user_id se shard, receipts ka write path async queue se batch, purane records cold storage mein.
advanced.production_improvements: Outbox pattern, TTL-based partition drops, `(channel, provider_id)` index, raw events ka append-only log audit ke liye, aur read replica se GET /notifications.

question: The HTTP handlers rely on Node's single thread for idempotency. What exactly is guaranteed, and what breaks with two server instances?
answer_hinglish:
Guarantee: ek process ke andar, `POST /notifications` handler ka body ek synchronous block hai -- `getByKey`, `notify` (jo keys map check + record set + key set + enqueue karta hai), aur response. Event loop ek callback ko complete chalata hai phir agla. Toh do concurrent requests same key ke saath aayein, toh ek poora khatam hoga, phir doosra: pehla 202 paata hai, doosra 200 replay ya 409. Koi lock nahi chahiye kyunki interleaving possible hi nahi. Yahi reason hai ki handlers jaan-boojh ke synchronous rakhe gaye.

`applyReceipt` bhi synchronous hai, toh do webhooks same delivery ke liye ek saath aayein toh bhi merge ek ek karke hota hai -- aur waise bhi merge commutative hai.

Do instances par kya tootega: har instance ka apna `keys` LRU, apne records. Client ka retry load balancer doosre instance par gaya toh doosra instance key nahi jaanta -> duplicate notification, duplicate OTP. Webhook provider ne instance B ko maara jabki send instance A ne record kiya -> B ke liye woh unknown id hai, parked hi rahega aur 1 h mein expire. Aur GET /notifications/:id random 404 dega.

Fix: shared store with atomic primitives -- idempotency key ka `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` ya Redis `SET NX`, receipts ka conditional UPDATE. Jaise hi store async hua, `getByKey` aur `notify` ke beech `await` aayega, toh new-vs-replay ka decision bhi atomic insert ke result se lena padega, alag read se nahi. Stage 2 ka worker side (leases, lease token check, provider idempotency key) already multi-process ke liye design hua hai; HTTP side ka in-memory shortcut nahi.
why_needed: Node mein 'race nahi ho sakti' aadha sach hai -- sirf sync code ke andar aur sirf ek process mein. Interviewer yahi boundary check karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter, ek clerk: line mein log ek ek karke aate hain, koi do token ek saath nahi le sakta. Do counter khol do bina shared register ke, toh ek hi aadmi dono counters se token le lega.
how_it_works: Event loop run-to-completion: sync function ke beech koi aur JS nahi chalta. Await / callback point par hi doosre requests ghus sakte hain.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts` header comment: handlers synchronous on purpose. POST handler comment: "Both calls are synchronous, so nothing can run between them". `QueuedNotifier.notify` comment: "Synchronous: validates, stores the record, queues the jobs, returns the record". Multi-instance support is NOT built here; README stage 2 known list aur PLAN in-memory clearly batate hain.

Code simple, reasoning simple
Receipt merge kisi bhi interleaving mein sahi
disadvantages: Horizontal scaling ke liye yeh guarantee kaam nahi aati
Ek future `await` chupchaap race khol sakta hai
common_mistakes: Yeh maan lena ki Node mein races hoti hi nahi
Async store ke saath read-then-write idempotency
Sticky sessions ko idempotency ka solution samajhna
follow_up_questions: How would a test catch a race introduced by an await?
Would sticky load balancing fix the duplicate problem?
Which parts of stage 2 already tolerate multiple processes?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sync handlers ek strong local guarantee dete hain par horizontal scaling block karte hain jab tak state shared na ho. Shared store se scaling milti hai par har request ek network hop + atomic op.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Do instances bina shared keys: retry doosre instance par -> duplicate send. Webhook wrong instance par -> receipt kabhi apply nahi. Instance restart -> keys gone, 24 h window toot jaati hai.
advanced.alternatives: Sticky routing by idempotency key hash (fragile, rebalancing par tootta), shared Redis, ya DB unique constraint (sabse robust).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par shared Redis/DB idempotency; 100x par key-space partitioning, aur provider-side idempotency keys (stage 2 wale) last line of defence ki tarah.

question: A provider's webhook can arrive before the worker has recorded the send result. How does the code handle that race, and why answer 202?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh real race hai: worker provider ko call karta hai, provider message accept karke turant (ya bahut jaldi) delivered/bounced webhook bhej deta hai -- aur hamare worker ka `await` abhi provider ka response process hi kar raha hai. Webhook ko lagta hai yeh provider id kisi ka nahi. 404 de do toh? PLAN.md ka jawab: "not every provider retries a 4xx" -- receipt hamesha ke liye kho jaayega.

Isliye unknown `<channel>:<providerId>` ka receipt **park** hota hai: cache-kit `LruCache` mein (default 1 h TTL, 10 000 entries), aur agar wahi key ke kai receipts pehle aa gaye toh woh bhi `mergeReceipt` se merge hote hain, overwrite nahi. HTTP 202 `{ result: "parked" }` -- "maine le liya, baad mein lagaunga". 200 nahi kyunki abhi apply nahi hua; provider ke liye dono success hain, toh woh retry nahi karega.

Jab worker send record karta hai, har accepted provider id ke liye `sentBy` set karta hai aur `parked.get(key)` check karta hai; mila toh delivery par merge, parked se delete, `receiptsApplied++`.

Test isse deterministic banata hai: `push.willAnswer(() => { ...applyReceipt("push", "early-1", bounced) ... applyReceipt("push", "early-1", delivered) ...; return { status: "sent", providerId: "early-1" } })` -- receipts fake provider ke andar, send result se pehle. Expected: dono `parked`, final receipt bounced (merge), baad wala delivered `unchanged`. README note: yeh test pehle delivered phir bounced bhejta tha, jo 'last one wins' bug bhi pass kar deta; ab bounced pehle bhejta hai. Mutation 'parked answered 200' bhi pakda gaya.
why_needed: Fast providers ke saath yeh race rare nahi hai, aur 404 se receipt chupchaap gayab ho jaata.
real_world_analogy: Courier ka 'delivered' SMS aa gaya par office ne abhi parcel register mein entry nahi ki. Clerk SMS phenkta nahi, ek tray mein rakhta hai; entry hote hi tray dekhta hai.
how_it_works: Unknown key -> parked.set(key, merge(parked.get(key), r)) -> 202. Send recorded -> sentBy.set; early = parked.get; merge; parked.delete.
in_this_project: `src/queued-notifier.ts` `applyReceipt` aur sent branch. `src/http/app.ts`: `res.status(result === "parked" ? 202 : 200).json({ result })`. Tests: receipts.test.ts 'a receipt that beats the send result is parked, then applied when the send is recorded', 'an unknown id stays parked only for the TTL' (`parkTtlMs: 60_000`, `clock.advance(60_001)`), http.test.ts 'a receipt for a send not recorded yet -> 202 parked'.

Provider retry behaviour par depend nahi
Merge rule parked receipts par bhi same
disadvantages: Garbage / random ids bhi 1 h tak memory lete hain (bounded 10 000)
Parked ka in-memory hona: restart par gone
Kabhi match na hone wale receipts ka koi alert nahi
common_mistakes: Unknown id par 404 dena
Parked entry ko overwrite karna
Parked receipt apply karke delete bhool jaana (double count)

Could a signed attacker fill the parked cache?
Why 202 rather than 200 for parked?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Parked full (10 000) -> LRU sabse purana gira deta hai, woh receipt khoya. Worker ka send result 1 h se zyada late (stuck job) -> parked expire. Process restart -> sab parked gone. Webhook alag instance par -> wahan kabhi match nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Provider ko 409/425 lauta ke retry karwana; receipts ek durable inbound queue mein daalna aur async consumer se apply karna jo id na mile toh delay ke saath retry kare; ya send se pehle provider id reserve karna (sab providers support nahi karte).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x par parked table DB mein (expires_at index), ya inbound receipts queue jiska consumer retry-with-delay karta hai; LRU size per instance nahi, global capacity plan.

question: Why is the API key checked before the body is parsed, and why is there a 64 KB body limit?
answer_hinglish:
Middleware order Express mein execution order hai. `createApp` mein API-key middleware `app.use(express.json(...))` se PEHLE registered hai. Matlab bina key ka request JSON parse tak pahunchta hi nahi -- 401 turant. Test isse lock karta hai: 'broken JSON without a key is 401, not 400'. Mutation 'auth removed or moved after body parsing' pakda gaya.

Performance angle: body parse karna kaam hai -- bytes padhna, buffer karna, `JSON.parse` (jo synchronous hai aur event loop block karta hai). Ek unauthenticated attacker ko yeh kaam free mein nahi milna chahiye. Pehle sasta check (ek header, ek SHA-256, ek compare), phir mehenga kaam. Security angle bhi same: jo request authorised nahi, uska content parser ke bugs tak nahi pahunchta.

64 KB limit (`bodyLimit` default "64kb") isliye: ek notification request chhota hota hai (`typeId`, `userId`, kuch template data). Bina limit ke koi 100 MB body bhej ke memory aur `JSON.parse` time kha sakta hai. Limit cross -> body-parser `entity.too.large` -> 413 `BODY_TOO_LARGE`. Test `bodyLimit: "1kb"` ke saath 2 000 characters ka pad bhejta hai aur 413 dekhta hai.

Webhook route ka bhi same limit hai (`express.raw({ type: "application/json", limit: bodyLimit })`), aur wahan bhi signature JSON parse se pehle check hota hai. Is project mein koi benchmark nahi hai; point yeh hai ki rejection sasta ho aur pehle ho.
why_needed: Mehenga kaam sirf un requests par karo jo uske laayak hain; warna ek simple flood bhi CPU aur memory kha jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Club ke bouncer pehle ID dekhta hai, phir andar jaane deta hai. Bina ID wale ka bag check karne mein time waste nahi karta. Aur bada trunk le ke aaye toh gate par hi mana.
how_it_works: Middleware chain: webhook route (raw) -> auth -> express.json(limit) -> routes. Auth fail -> throw HttpError(401) -> error handler; body kabhi parse nahi.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts`: comment "Auth first: an unauthenticated caller gets 401 before its body is even parsed." `AppOptions.bodyLimit` default `"64kb"`. Tests in `test/http.test.ts`: '401 comes before the body is parsed', 'not JSON -> 415; over the body limit -> 413'.

Memory per request bounded
Parser attack surface chhota
disadvantages: Bade legit payloads (bulk send) ke liye limit badhani padegi
Limit per-route nahi, ek hi
common_mistakes: express.json ko globally sabse pehle lagana
Body limit hata dena 'kyunki internal API hai'
413 ko 400 bana dena

question: How is the API key handled: where it comes from, its minimum length, and why it is compared via SHA-256 digests and timingSafeEqual?
answer_hinglish:
Teen rules hain. **Source**: key sirf environment variable `NOTIFY_API_KEY` se aati hai -- code ya repo mein kabhi nahi. `main.ts` bina key (ya 16 se chhoti) ke `process.exit(1)` karta hai. **Length**: `createApp` khud bhi check karta hai, `MIN_API_KEY_LENGTH = 16`, chhoti key par `RangeError` -- koi "open mode" nahi. Test: `""`, `"short"`, `undefined` teeno throw, 16 x wali key chalti hai.

**Constant-time compare**: normal `===` pehle mismatched character par ruk jaata hai, toh galat guess kitni jaldi reject hua usse attacker byte-by-byte key guess kar sakta hai (timing attack). Network par yeh noise mein mushkil hai par impossible nahi, aur fix sasta hai. `timingSafeEqual` poore buffer ko compare karta hai -- par woh dono buffers same length maangta hai, warna throw. Agar raw key compare karte toh length check karna padta, aur length mismatch ka fast path key ki LENGTH leak karta. Isliye dono taraf SHA-256 digest: hamesha 32 bytes, toh na content leak hota hai na length. Expected digest `createApp` mein ek baar banta hai.

Header format strict hai: `/^Bearer (.+)$/` -- `bearer` (lowercase), bina "Bearer " ke raw key, `"Bearer "` khaali -- sab 401 (test mein 5 bad headers). Response message hamesha same "missing or wrong API key", toh kya galat tha yeh bhi nahi batata. Limitation: ek shared key, per-caller keys / scopes / rotation nahi bane -- PLAN.md: "a real deployment would add per-caller keys and scopes".
why_needed: Notification API ke paas SMS aur email bhejne ki taakat hai -- iski key leak ya guess hui toh spam aur cost dono.
real_world_analogy: Locker ka combination check karne wala agar pehla galat digit dekhte hi beep kare, toh chor digit by digit try karke khol lega. Achha lock poora combination check karke hi jawab deta hai, aur yeh bhi nahi batata ki combination kitne digits ka hai.
how_it_works: Startup: expected = sha256(apiKey). Request: header regex -> sha256(presented) -> timingSafeEqual(expected, presented) (dono 32 bytes).
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts`: `MIN_API_KEY_LENGTH`, `digest`, `keyMatches`, aur `createApp` ka RangeError. `src/main.ts` env check. Tests: 'no key, a wrong key, or the key without Bearer -> 401, and nothing is queued', 'refuses to start without a real key'. Mutations caught: 'Bearer optional', 'key length boundary'.

Koi open mode nahi, weak key startup par reject
Key repo mein kabhi nahi
disadvantages: Ek shared key: kaun sa caller, pata nahi
Rotation ke liye restart / downtime
TLS is process mein nahi (HOST default 127.0.0.1)

Raw buffers par timingSafeEqual (length mismatch par throw / leak)
Dev ke liye default key code mein rakh dena

Why does the digest hide the key's length?
Is hashing the key at rest needed here?

question: Explain the webhook signature: what is signed, why the raw body, why a 5 minute tolerance, and why the route is registered before the API-key check.
answer_hinglish:
Provider ke paas hamari API key nahi hai (aur hona bhi nahi chahiye), toh woh khud ko ek per-provider shared secret se prove karta hai -- Stripe scheme. Header: `Notify-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, jahan hex = `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>." + raw body)`. Secret per channel env se: `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PUSH` / `_SMS` / `_EMAIL`; jis channel ka secret nahi, uska webhook 404.

**Raw body kyun**: signature exact bytes par hai. Agar pehle JSON parse karke dobara stringify karo toh spacing, key order, number format badal sakte hain aur valid signature fail hoga. Isliye route `express.raw({ type: "application/json" })` use karta hai, Buffer milta hai. Test: provider ki apni spacing aur key order wala body bhi applied.

**Timestamp signed + 5 min tolerance**: bina timestamp ke ek captured valid request hamesha replay ho sakta. `t` HMAC ke andar hai, toh attacker use badal nahi sakta, aur `Math.abs(now - t*1000) > 5 min` -> refuse (aage ka time bhi). Exact edge dono taraf tested.

**Verify before parse**: unsigned garbage kabhi `JSON.parse` tak nahi pahunchta -- test: unsigned `{` 401, signed `{` 400.

**Before API-key middleware**: providers ke paas key nahi, toh route pehle registered hai; aur ulta bhi -- API key yahan accepted NAHI (test mein Bearer key ke saath 401). Har secret alag, toh email ka secret push webhook ke liye fail. Parsing strict: header regex anchored `^t=(\d{1,12}),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$`, toh `timingSafeEqual` hamesha 32 vs 32 bytes compare karta hai.
why_needed: Unsigned webhook endpoint matlab koi bhi kisi bhi delivery ko bounced/delivered mark kar sakta -- status, metrics aur future suppression sab poisoned.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka cheque: signature (HMAC) amount aur date (body + t) dono par hai. Purani date ka cheque (5 min se zyada) bank nahi leta, aur cheque ki photocopy (re-serialized JSON) par signature match nahi karta.

in_this_project: `src/receipts.ts`: `signWebhook`, `verifyWebhook`, `SIGNATURE_HEADER`, `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_MS = 5 * 60_000`. `src/http/app.ts` webhook route (404 no secret -> 415 not Buffer -> 401 signature -> 400 JSON / INVALID_RECEIPT). `createApp` weak (<16) ya unknown-channel secrets par RangeError. Tests: receipts.test.ts signatures (wrong secret, changed body, changed time, tolerance edges, 8 malformed headers); http.test.ts '5 ways to be 401'. Per-provider secrets: ek leak doosre ko nahi chhoota

question: Give a threat model for this notification API: what do the current controls stop, and what do they not?
answer_hinglish:
Jo controls rokte hain: (1) **Unauthenticated callers** -- API key required, constant-time, auth body parse se pehle; koi open mode nahi. (2) **Forged receipts** -- per-provider HMAC over timestamp + raw body. (3) **Replays of captured webhooks** -- 5 min tolerance. (4) **Large-body abuse** -- 64 KB limit. (5) **Info leaks** -- 500 ka message chhupa, `x-powered-by` disabled, ek fixed 401 message. (6) **Accidental exposure** -- `HOST` default 127.0.0.1. (7) **Bad input crashing state** -- shape checks (PreferenceStore TypeError fix), aur error = kuch store nahi.

Jo NAHI rokta -- honest list: **Leaked key = full access**: ek shared key, koi scopes nahi (jo OTP bhej sakta hai woh marketing bhi aur preferences badal bhi sakta hai), koi per-caller audit nahi. **Confused deputy / IDOR**: API `userId` par trust karti hai; caller service ko khud check karna hai ki end user wahi hai -- PLAN.md aur inbox comment yahi bolte hain. **Abuse by a valid caller**: koi per-caller rate limit nahi; marketing frequency caps (stage 2) per user hain, transactional par nahi -- ek buggy caller loop mein OTP spam kar sakta hai. **No TLS** in-process: production mein reverse proxy / mesh chahiye. **Key rotation** nahi. **Replay within 5 min**: possible, par merge rule idempotent hai toh asar zero. **Parked cache flooding** sirf valid signature wala kar sakta hai.

Production ke liye: per-caller keys (hashed at rest) + scopes (`notify:transactional`, `preferences:write`), per-caller rate limits (ratelimit-kit yahin reuse ho sakta), per-user transactional caps (OTP 5/min), TLS, rotation with two active keys, audit log.
why_needed: Senior round mein 'secure hai?' ka jawab haan/na nahi hota -- kis attacker ke against, aur kya bacha hai, yeh batana hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Building mein main gate par guard hai (API key) aur service entrance par alag pass (webhook secret). Par guard ke paas ek hi master pass list hai, aur andar har room par lock nahi -- master pass wala kahin bhi ja sakta hai.
how_it_works: Layers: network (127.0.0.1 default) -> auth (key / HMAC) -> size limit -> parse -> shape checks -> library rules. Gaps authorization (scopes, user ownership) aur abuse limits mein hain.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts`: `app.disable("x-powered-by")`, `keyMatches`, webhook route before auth, `toHttp` hiding 500s, inbox comment "The caller (the app's backend) must check that the logged-in user IS :userId". `src/main.ts`: HOST default 127.0.0.1. PLAN.md: "No CORS, no per-user login; a real deployment would add per-caller keys and scopes."
advantages: Authentication aur webhook integrity solid
Defaults safe (no open mode, localhost bind)
Gaps documented, chhupaaye nahi
disadvantages: Authorization coarse (ek key = sab)
Per-caller abuse limits nahi
Rotation aur audit nahi
common_mistakes: Authentication ko authorization samajhna
Service API key ko end-user identity maan lena
Transactional messages ko rate limits se bahar rakhna bina kisi cap ke
follow_up_questions: How would you design scopes for this API?
How do you rate limit OTPs per user without blocking real logins?
Where would you terminate TLS?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek shared key simple ops hai par blast radius poora system. Per-caller keys + scopes key management laate hain par leak ka asar ek caller tak.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Key leak -> SMS spam aur cost; buggy caller loop -> user ko 100 OTP; compromised caller -> kisi bhi user ki preferences badalna; webhook secret leak -> fake bounces se status/metrics poison.
advanced.alternatives: OAuth2 client credentials (JWT with scopes), mTLS between services, API gateway par auth + rate limiting, ya service mesh identity (SPIFFE).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x callers: key registry DB mein, hashed keys, per-key quotas. 100x: gateway layer, centralized auth, per-tenant isolation.
advanced.production_improvements: Scopes, per-caller + per-user transactional rate limits, audit log (kaun, kab, kis user ko), key rotation with overlap, anomaly alerts (achanak SMS volume), TLS everywhere.

question: What happens on Ctrl+C or SIGTERM, in what order does startServer's close() shut things down, and what is lost?
answer_hinglish:
`close()` ka order deliberate hai: **(1)** `server.close()` -- naye connections lena band, jo requests chal rahi hain woh finish hoti hain. **(2)** `server.closeIdleConnections()` -- keep-alive sockets jinpe koi request nahi, unhe band karo, warna `server.close()` ka callback unke timeout tak latka rehta. **(3)** `await closed` -- saari in-flight requests ka jawab chala gaya. **(4)** `await worker.stop()` -- stage 2 ka Worker naye jobs claim karna band karta hai aur jo send chal rahe hain unka wait karta hai.

Order kyun yeh? Agar worker pehle rukta, toh abhi chal rahi request ka `notify()` jobs queue karta aur koi unhe chalane wala nahi. HTTP pehle band, phir worker -- "pehle input band karo, phir pipeline khaali karo".

`close()` idempotent hai: `closing ??= (async () => ...)()` -- jitni baar bulao, ek hi shutdown promise. Test `expect(running.close()).toBe(running.close())`. `main.ts` ka signal handler `stopping` flag se doosra Ctrl+C ignore karta hai, success par `exit(0)`, error par `exit(1)`.

Kya lost hota hai: jo jobs QUEUED hain par claim nahi hue, aur saare records, keys, receipts -- sab memory mein the. server.ts comment honestly kehta hai real queue mein doosra process unhe utha leta. Doosri failure: port already in use -> `startServer` reject karta hai (`once("error", reject)`), process crash nahi. Signal handler khud test mein nahi hai (README); `startServer().close()` tested hai real timers ke saath -- ek gated slow send ke saath, close tab tak resolve nahi hota jab tak send khatam na ho.
why_needed: Deploys aur autoscaling har din processes ko SIGTERM bhejte hain. Bina graceful shutdown ke aadhi requests 502 aur aadhe sends unknown state mein.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan band karte waqt pehle shutter aadha giraate ho (naye customer nahi), andar wale ka bill banate ho, phir kitchen ka chalta order poora karke gas band karte ho.
how_it_works: server.close -> closeIdleConnections -> await closed -> worker.stop (waits for in-flight sends). Memoized via ??=.
in_this_project: `src/http/server.ts` `startServer` / `RunningServer.close`. `src/main.ts` SIGINT/SIGTERM handler. `test/server.test.ts`: 'serves, its worker sends; close() waits for the send in progress, then the port is closed' (`slow` gate, `closed` false after 30 ms, true after resolve, then fetch rejects) aur 'a port already in use rejects instead of crashing' (`/EADDRINUSE/`). Mutations caught: startServer not waiting for the worker, closing twice, not rejecting on a port in use.

Ek hi shutdown, double signal safe
Port conflict par clean reject
disadvantages: Queued jobs aur poora state memory ke saath gone
Koi shutdown deadline nahi: ek atka send close ko rok sakta hai (send timeout stage 2 bound karta hai)
common_mistakes: Worker ko HTTP se pehle rokna
closeIdleConnections bhool jaana (shutdown latakta hai)
Signal par seedha process.exit

question: An email bounces after it was sent. What does the system do today, what does it not do, and how would you build the missing parts?
answer_hinglish:
Aaj: provider `bounced` webhook bhejta hai -> signature verify -> `applyReceipt` -> delivery par `receipt: { event: "bounced", at }`. `notificationStatus` us sent delivery ko `failed` gin leta hai. Agar notification ke doosre channel (jaise push) sent hain aur bounce nahi hue, overall status `delivered`; agar sab bounce / fail toh `failed`. Late `delivered` bounce ko undo nahi kar sakta (merge rule). Bas itna.

Kya NAHI bana (README aur PLAN dono mein listed): **(1) Bounce ke baad fallback** -- OTP SMS bounce hua toh email par nahi jaata. **(2) Suppression list** -- bounced address par agli baar bhi bhejenge, jo email reputation ke liye bura hai (providers zyada bounce rate par account throttle karte hain). **(3) opened / clicked** events.

Main kaise banaunga: **Fallback**: sirf `first` mode, aur sirf tab jab notification abhi "useful" ho (OTP 5 min baad bekaar). Receipt apply hone par agar delivery bounced aur record `first` mode, toh `queueNextCandidate` jaisa next channel enqueue -- par `not_needed` deliveries ko wapas `pending` banana padega, aur ek deadline (`fallbackUntil`) chahiye. Idempotent rehna chahiye: bounce do baar aaye toh fallback ek baar -- yeh merge ke `applied` vs `unchanged` se naturally milta hai, sirf `applied` par trigger. **Suppression**: `(channel, address)` table, hard bounce par insert; planner mein address skip ka ek naya `skipReason` (jaise `suppressed_address`); soft bounce (mailbox full) ko count karke threshold. Transactional bhi suppress hoga, kyunki address hi dead hai. **opened/clicked**: alag fields, rank ladder mein nahi.
why_needed: Bounces ignore karne se ek taraf user ko message nahi milta, doosri taraf sender reputation girti hai aur provider throttle karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Chitthi 'address not found' ke saath wapas aayi. Aaj system bas register mein 'wapas aayi' likhta hai. Achha system phone kar leta (fallback) aur address book mein us pate par laal nishaan laga deta (suppression).
how_it_works: Today: receipt -> merge -> status derivation. Missing: receipt-applied hook -> fallback job / suppression insert.
in_this_project: `src/record.ts` `notificationStatus` (sent + bounced -> failed). `src/queued-notifier.ts` `applyReceipt`. Test 'a bounce makes the notification failed unless another channel still counts as delivered'. README receipts: "Not built: falling back to the next channel after a bounce, a suppression list (stop sending to an address that bounced), opened / clicked events".
advantages: Status bounce ko sach mein reflect karta hai
Merge rule fallback trigger ko idempotent banane ka base deta hai
Gaps clearly documented
disadvantages: User tak message pahunchane ki koi koshish bounce ke baad nahi
Bad addresses par repeat sends
Engagement data nahi
common_mistakes: Har bounce par fallback (stale OTP bhi)
Soft aur hard bounce ko same treat karna
Duplicate bounce receipt par do baar fallback
follow_up_questions: How do you distinguish soft from hard bounces?
Should a transactional email be suppressed?
Where does the fallback deadline come from?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Fallback-after-bounce delivery badhata hai par duplicate risk laata hai (bounce galat tha toh user ko do messages). Suppression reputation bachata hai par galat hard bounce ek valid user ko chup kara deta hai -- un-suppress flow chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Provider ka bounce webhook ghanton late: fallback bekaar (OTP expired). Bounce receipt park hua aur expire: na status update na suppression. Suppression table down: send rokna ya bina check bhejna -- policy decide karni padegi.
advanced.alternatives: Provider ki apni suppression lists (SES account-level), fallback sirf send-time failures par (aaj jaisa), ya user ko app mein 'email bounced, update karo' prompt.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 100x par suppression check har send par ek lookup -- in-memory bloom filter / cache ke saath DB; bounce events ek stream se aggregate.
advanced.production_improvements: Hard/soft bounce classification per provider, suppression table with reason + expiry, fallback with deadline per notification type, bounce-rate alert per provider, user-facing address fix flow.

question: PUT /users/u1/preferences with {"mutedMarketing": [], "quietHours": null} returned a 500 instead of a 422. How would you investigate and fix it?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh real bug tha jo stage 3 mein mila. **Symptom**: ek well-formed par galat body par 500 `INTERNAL`, jabki caller ki galti thi (422 hona chahiye).

**Investigate**: 500 hamesha log hota hai (`toHttp` ka default branch: "notification API: unexpected error"), toh pehle log dekho -- ek `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'start')`. Yeh `NotificationError` nahi hai, isliye mapping table tak pahuncha hi nahi aur default 500 bana. Stack trace `PreferenceStore.set` ki taraf le jaata hai.

**Cause**: stage 1 mein `set()` typed input maan ke likha tha -- `Preferences` TypeScript type kehta hai quietHours ya toh object hai ya undefined. Andar `if (prefs.quietHours !== undefined) parseHhMm(prefs.quietHours.start)` -- `null` undefined nahi hai, toh `null.start` -> TypeError. Library ke callers TypeScript the, isliye kabhi nahi hua; HTTP se aaya JSON koi type promise nahi karta. Compile-time types runtime par exist nahi karte.

**Smallest fix**: `set()` mein shape check -- `prefs === null || typeof prefs !== "object"` -> INVALID_PREFERENCES; mutedMarketing array of channels; quietHours undefined ho sakta hai, par agar diya toh `null` ya non-object -> INVALID_PREFERENCES. Comment: "Input may come straight from an HTTP body (stage 3), so the shape is checked, not assumed."

**Proof**: policy.test.ts mein ek naya test (`null`, non-objects, `quietHours: null`), aur http.test.ts 'invalid preferences -> 422 and the stored ones are kept' -- 4 bad bodies 422 aur stored `["sms"]` wahi rehta hai. Lesson: trust boundary par validate karo, chahe andar types hon.
why_needed: Caller ki galti par 500 do toh caller retry karta rahega aur hamare alerts jhoothe bajenge; asli bug (missing validation) chhupa rehta.
real_world_analogy: Form par 'date of birth' ka khana khaali chhoda aur office ka computer crash ho gaya. Galti form bharne wale ki thi, par crash office ki kamzori hai -- computer ko 'yeh khana zaroori hai' bolna chahiye tha.
how_it_works: Unknown error -> default 500 + log. Fix: error library ke apne type (NotificationError INVALID_PREFERENCES) mein convert, jo STATUS_BY_CODE se 422 banta hai.
in_this_project: `src/preferences.ts` `PreferenceStore.set` (shape checks). `src/http/app.ts` PUT route: `requireUser` -> `requireJson` -> `preferences.set(userId, req.body)`. Tests: `test/http.test.ts` 'invalid preferences -> 422 and the stored ones are kept; not JSON -> 415' (raw `null` body 400 INVALID_JSON kyunki express.json strict hai). README table: policy.test.ts +1.

Status code sahi (422)
Stored preferences invalid input par untouched
disadvantages: Har public method mein manual shape checks verbose hain
common_mistakes: TypeScript types ko runtime validation samajhna
Fix sirf HTTP handler mein lagana
500 ko 422 mein badalne ke liye generic catch-all

question: A new provider integration gets 401 INVALID_SIGNATURE on every webhook even though the secret is right. What do you check?
answer_hinglish:
401 INVALID_SIGNATURE ek hi code hai chaar alag causes ke liye -- jaan-boojh ke, attacker ko hint nahi dena. Toh debugging hamare side par systematic honi chahiye.

**1. Header format.** `verifyWebhook` ka regex anchored hai: `^t=(\d{1,12}),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$`. Uppercase hex, spaces (`t=1, v1=...`), extra fields, `v2=`, ya milliseconds wala 13-digit `t` -- sab fail. Test mein 8 malformed headers hain, inme se ek leading space aur ek extra `,x=1` bhi.

**2. Timestamp units aur clock.** `t` unix SECONDS hai. Provider ne ms bheja toh 13 digits -> regex fail. Seconds sahi par server clock drift 5 min se zyada -> tolerance fail. `date` aur NTP check karo.

**3. Kya sign hua.** HMAC input `"<t>." + raw body` hai. Provider ne sirf body sign ki, ya `t` aur body ke beech dot nahi, ya body sign karne ke baad pretty-print karke bheji -> mismatch. Hamare side par: agar kisi ne route ke aage `express.json()` laga diya ho, raw bytes milenge hi nahi. Isliye route `express.raw({ type: "application/json" })` use karta hai aur auth/json middleware se pehle registered hai.

**4. Galat secret / channel.** `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_EMAIL` ka secret push URL par -> 401 (test: "another channel's secret"). Trailing newline env file mein bhi secret badal deta hai.

Tool: `signWebhook(secret, rawBody, nowMs)` exported hai -- provider ka exact body aur time le ke apna header banao, unke header se compare karo. Match nahi toh unka signing galat; match hai toh hamara transport (proxy body badal raha hai?).
why_needed: Webhook integrations ka sabse common day-one problem yahi hai, aur generic 401 ki wajah se blind debugging hoti hai.
real_world_analogy: Taala aur chaabi dono sahi lag rahe hain par khul nahi raha: check karo chaabi ulti to nahi, taala badla to nahi, ya kisi ne chaabi ko ghis to nahi diya (body re-serialize).
how_it_works: Recompute locally with signWebhook; compare part by part: header format, t units, signed string, secret bytes.
in_this_project: `src/receipts.ts` `signWebhook` / `verifyWebhook` / `SIGNATURE_HEADER` ("notify-signature"). `src/http/app.ts` webhook route uses `express.raw` and `req.get(SIGNATURE_HEADER)`. Tests: receipts.test.ts 'malformed headers are refused, not thrown on'; http.test.ts 'the signature is over the raw bytes: spacing and key order the provider chose are fine'. `src/main.ts` reads `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_<CHANNEL>`.

Strict regex galat formats turant pakad leta hai
Generic 401 attacker ko hint nahi deta
disadvantages: Generic error se integrators ko confusion
Strict format = provider ka thoda alag format bhi fail

Seconds ki jagah ms timestamp
Env file mein secret ke saath newline
Debug ke liye 401 response mein expected signature bhej dena

question: Why are the Express handlers synchronous on purpose, and what would you do if a handler had to await something?
answer_hinglish:
Express 4 ka ek important behaviour: route handler ke andar synchronous `throw` Express pakad leta hai aur error handler tak bhejta hai. Par agar handler `async` hai aur promise reject hota hai, Express 4 use nahi dekhta -- request latki rehti hai (client timeout) aur Node `unhandledRejection` deta hai, jo process crash bhi kar sakta hai settings ke hisaab se. Express 5 yeh fix karta hai, Express 4 nahi.

Is project mein synchronous rehna free tha: stage 2 ka `QueuedNotifier.notify()` await nahi karta -- woh validate karke record store karta hai aur jobs queue karta hai; asli sending worker async mein karta hai. `applyReceipt`, `get`, preferences sab sync. Toh handlers bhi sync hain, aur har error -- HttpError, NotificationError -- seedha `throw` se error handler tak pahunchta hai. Bonus: sync hone se getByKey-before-notify trick race-free hai.

Agar await chahiye hota (DB, Redis), toh options: (1) **Express 5** par jaana -- rejected promises native `next(err)` tak jaate hain. (2) Ek chhota wrapper: `const wrap = (fn) => (req, res, next) => fn(req, res, next).catch(next)`. (3) `express-async-errors` jaisa monkey-patch (recommend nahi karunga, hidden magic). Main Express 5 ya wrapper chunta.

Trade-off: sync rule ek constraint hai jo future developer ko pata hona chahiye -- isliye file header mein comment hai. Aur await aate hi idempotency logic ko atomic store-level operation chahiye, sirf error handling nahi badalti.
why_needed: Async error handling Express 4 ki classic trap hai -- ek rejected promise = latki request + possibly crashed process.
real_world_analogy: Class mein teacher sirf haath uthane wale (sync throw) ko dekhti hai; jo baad mein chitthi bhejta hai (rejected promise) uski baat kabhi nahi sunti jab tak koi chitthi ko haath mein na pakdaye (wrapper / Express 5).
how_it_works: Sync throw -> Express Layer try/catch -> next(err) -> 4-arg handler. Async reject -> Express 4 ke try/catch se bahar -> unhandled.
in_this_project: `src/http/app.ts` header: "The handlers are synchronous on purpose: QueuedNotifier.notify() does not await (stage 2), and in Express 4 a synchronous throw reaches the error handler while a rejected promise would not." PLAN.md stage 3: "Express 4, synchronous handlers." `package.json`: `"express": "4.22.3"`.
advantages: Har error guaranteed error handler tak
Koi wrapper / patch nahi
Idempotency trick race-free
disadvantages: Hidden constraint: future await se behaviour toot sakta hai
Async I/O wale features ke liye refactor chahiye
common_mistakes: Express 4 mein async handler bina catch ke
try/catch har handler mein copy-paste
Yeh maan lena ki Express 4 promises samajhta hai
follow_up_questions: What changes in Express 5's error handling?
Why not just add express-async-errors?
How would a test catch a hanging async handler?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sync handlers Express 4 ke saath sabse simple aur safe hain par sirf tab possible jab library sync ho. Express 5 move dependency risk laata hai par async ko first-class banata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Koi developer `async` laga de aur andar throw ho: request hang, client timeout, aur bina unhandledRejection handler ke process crash -- saari in-flight requests ke saath.
advanced.alternatives: Express 5, Fastify (async native, schema validation), Hono / Koa. Ya wrapper function jo har route par explicit ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale par asli farak async I/O se aata hai (DB) -- tab sync constraint tootna hi hai, toh woh migration plan ka hissa ho.
advanced.production_improvements: Lint rule (no async route handlers bina wrap), `process.on("unhandledRejection")` logging, ek test jo async throw par 500 expect kare, aur Express 5 migration evaluate karna.

question: Why is PUT /users/:userId/preferences a whole replacement and not a merge, and why only for known users?
answer_hinglish:
**PUT = replace**: jo caller bhejta hai, wahi store hota hai -- `{ mutedMarketing: ["sms"] }` bheja aur pehle quietHours set the, toh ab quietHours nahi rahenge. Response 200 mein wahi lautata hai jo store hua (`preferences.get`). Kyun? PUT ka HTTP meaning yahi hai (idempotent full replacement), aur caller ka mental model simple: "settings screen ka poora state bhejo". Merge (PATCH) mein sawaal aate hain: field hatana ho toh `null` bhejo? missing ka matlab "unchanged" ya "remove"? Bugs wahi se aate hain. Is project mein PATCH bana hi nahi.

**Known users only**: `requireUser(userId)` -> `users.get` nahi mila toh 404 `NOT_FOUND`, aur kuch store nahi. Kyun? PLAN.md: "Storing preferences for a typo'd user id would silently never apply." Caller ko lagta mute ho gaya, par asli user ko marketing aati rehti -- woh bhi silently. 404 galti turant dikha deta hai.

Yeh H15 se aaya: mutation checks mein 'the user check removed (PUT)' survive kar gaya -- matlab koi test PUT unknown user nahi bhejta tha. Test add hua: 'PUT preferences for an unknown user -> 404 and nothing stored (a typo'd id would never apply)' -- `preferences.get("ghost")` default `{ mutedMarketing: [] }` hi rehta hai.

Order bhi dekho: PUT route mein `requireUser` -> `requireJson` -> `set`. Invalid preferences par 422 aur purani stored values untouched (validation pehle, phir write).
why_needed: Preferences legal/consent jaisi cheez hain -- galat user par chupchaap save hona ya half-merge, dono user ko galat messages bhejte hain.
real_world_analogy: Form dobara bharna (PUT) vs purane form par overwriting karna (PATCH). Aur galat roll number par form jama karne par office ko mana karna chahiye, chupchaap file mein nahi daalna.

question: Why does this project pin Express 4.22.3 instead of 4.21.2, and how do you treat dependency advisories for a runtime dependency?
answer_hinglish:
Project 20 (cache-kit) ke tests Express 4.21.2 use karte the. Yahan bhi wahi lene ka socha, par `npm audit` ne dikhaya ki 4.21.2 ki transitive dependencies -- `body-parser`, `path-to-regexp`, `qs` -- par published advisories hain. Farak context ka hai: project 20 mein Express sirf devDependency tha (tests), yahan Express RUNTIME dependency hai -- har incoming request inhi libraries se guzarti hai. `path-to-regexp` route matching karta hai (ReDoS-type issues ka history), `qs` query strings parse karta hai, `body-parser` bodies. Yeh sab untrusted input ke pehle touch point hain.

Isliye `package.json` mein exact `"express": "4.22.3"` (caret nahi), aur README: `npm audit --omit=dev`: 0. `--omit=dev` isliye ki production mein jo ship hota hai uska audit chahiye; dev tools (vitest) ka advisory alag priority par.

Production process jo main follow karunga: (1) exact pins + lockfile + `npm ci`, taaki build reproducible ho. (2) CI mein `npm audit --omit=dev` -- high/critical par fail. (3) Advisory aaye toh dekho: kya hamara code woh path use karta hai? Runtime + network-facing = jaldi upgrade. (4) Patch upgrade ke baad poora test suite (yahan 192 tests) aur mutation-checked HTTP tests regression guard hain. (5) Dependabot / Renovate se automated PRs. Honest note: version number upgrade hai, koi behaviour change README mein noted nahi; tests ne 4.22.3 par pass kiya.
why_needed: Network-facing parsers attackers ka pehla target hain. 'Pichle project mein chal gaya' runtime dependency ke liye kaafi reason nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka main gate ka taala (runtime dep) aur store room ka taala (dev dep) -- dono mein crack ho toh pehle main gate badloge.
how_it_works: npm audit lockfile ke resolved versions ko advisory database se match karta hai; --omit=dev sirf production tree check karta hai.
in_this_project: `projects/21-notification/package.json`: `"express": "4.22.3"`. README stage 3: "Express 4.22.3, not the 4.21.2 used by project 20's tests: 4.21.2's body-parser, path-to-regexp and qs have published advisories, and here Express is a runtime dependency (npm audit --omit=dev: 0)." PLAN.md stage 3 decisions same.

npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high   # fail the build on high/critical advisories in what ships
npm test
